syllabus_version.title: CBSE Curriculum for the Academic Year 2026-27

book.title: Ganita Prakash-II
book.edition: NCERT (reprint year not stated in the prelims)

topics.title: Congruent figures: geometric twins

concepts.learning_objective: Students will define congruent figures as figures of the same shape and size that can be superimposed exactly, allowing rotation or flipping.
Students will identify which measurements fix the shape and size of a figure such as a two-arm symbol, a circle or a rectangle.

topics.title: The SSS condition and the convention for writing congruence

concepts.learning_objective: Students will use the SSS condition to decide whether two triangles are congruent.
Students will write a congruence statement so that corresponding vertices, sides and angles appear in matching order.

topics.title: Equal angles, the SAS condition and the SSA case

concepts.learning_objective: Students will explain why triangles with the same three angles have the same shape but need not be congruent.
Students will apply the SAS condition, including in figures with vertically opposite angles.
Students will show by construction that two sides and a non-included angle need not give congruent triangles.

topics.title: The ASA and AAS conditions

concepts.learning_objective: Students will apply the ASA condition using given or alternate angles and an included side.
Students will use the angle sum of a triangle to reduce the AAS case to ASA and conclude congruence.

topics.title: The RHS condition and choosing a congruence condition

concepts.learning_objective: Students will apply the RHS condition to right-angled triangles with equal hypotenuses and one other equal side.
Students will decide which sets of equal measurements (SSS, SAS, ASA, AAS, RHS) guarantee congruence and which do not.

topics.title: Angles of isosceles and equilateral triangles

concepts.learning_objective: Students will use congruence to show that angles opposite equal sides are equal and find unknown angles of isosceles triangles.
Students will deduce that every angle of an equilateral triangle measures 60 degrees.

topics.title: A Quick Recap of Integers

concepts.learning_objective: Find two integers when their sum and difference are given.
Model movements on a number line as integers with magnitude and direction and add them to find a final position.
Use tokens and zero pairs to show that subtracting an integer is the same as adding its additive inverse.

topics.title: Multiplication of Integers Using Tokens

concepts.learning_objective: Interpret a product with a positive multiplier as placing tokens into an empty bag repeatedly.
Interpret a product with a negative multiplier as removing tokens, using zero pairs when needed.

topics.title: Patterns, Sign Rules and Commutativity of Multiplication

concepts.learning_objective: State and apply the sign rules for the product of two integers, including Brahmagupta's rules.
Explain that 1 x a = a and (-1) x a = -a for every integer a.
Justify that integer multiplication is commutative, a x b = b x a.

topics.title: Using Integer Multiplication in Real Situations

concepts.learning_objective: Represent marks, profit and loss as integers and compute totals with multiplication and addition.
Represent rising, falling and descending quantities as integers and find the resulting position or value.

topics.title: Division of Integers

concepts.learning_objective: Rewrite an integer division as a missing-factor multiplication and solve it.
Apply the sign rules for the quotient of two integers.

topics.title: Expressions Using Integers

concepts.learning_objective: Recognise that integer multiplication is associative and that three or more integers can be multiplied in any order.
Find the sign of a product of many integers from the number of negative factors.
Apply the distributive property a x (b + c) = a x b + a x c to integers.

topics.title: The greatest of all: common factors and HCF

concepts.learning_objective: Find the common factors of two numbers by listing the factors of each.
Explain the Highest Common Factor (GCD) and use it to solve tiling, packing and jump problems.

topics.title: Primes and prime factorisation

concepts.learning_objective: Write a number as a product of primes and recognise that the prime factors are unique apart from order.
Use the division method to find the prime factorisation of a number.

topics.title: Factors from prime factorisation; conjectures

concepts.learning_objective: Construct the factors of a number from subparts of its prime factorisation.
Recognise a conjecture and disprove a false one with a counterexample.

topics.title: Finding the HCF using prime factorisation

concepts.learning_objective: Find the common factors and HCF of numbers as common subparts of their prime factorisations.
Find the HCF by taking each common prime the minimum number of times it occurs.

topics.title: Least, but not last: common multiples and LCM

concepts.learning_objective: Find the LCM as the lowest common multiple and apply it to repeating-event problems.
Find the LCM by taking each prime the maximum number of times it occurs in the factorisations.

topics.title: Patterns and properties of HCF and LCM

concepts.learning_objective: Make and justify general statements about the HCF and LCM of special pairs of numbers.
Find the HCF when numbers are doubled or are multiples of the same number.

topics.title: Efficient procedures and the HCF-LCM product property

concepts.learning_objective: Use the joint division procedure to find both the HCF and the LCM of two numbers.
Use the relation HCF x LCM = product of the two numbers.

topics.title: A Quick Recap of Decimals

concepts.learning_objective: Write decimal fractions with denominators 10, 100, 1000 and their sums as decimals using place value.
Divide a whole number by 10, 100 or 1000 by moving the decimal point to the left.

topics.title: Decimal Multiplication

concepts.learning_objective: Multiply decimals by multiplying the numbers without decimal points and placing the decimal point by counting decimal digits.
Predict whether a product of decimals is greater or less than the numbers multiplied.

topics.title: Decimal Division by 10, 100, 1000 and Equivalent Fractions

concepts.learning_objective: Divide a decimal by 10, 100 or 1000 by shifting the decimal point left.
Convert a fraction to a decimal by finding an equivalent fraction with denominator 10, 100, 1000 and so on.

topics.title: Long Division with Decimal Quotients, Dividends and Divisors

concepts.learning_objective: Use division by place value, regrouping Ones into Tenths and beyond, to find decimal quotients.
Divide by a decimal by multiplying the divisor and dividend by the same power of 10.

topics.title: Does This Ever End? Dividend, Divisor and Quotient

concepts.learning_objective: Recognise divisions whose decimal quotient never ends because remainders repeat.
Explore the repeating block 142857 of 1/7 and its cyclic multiples.
Compare the quotient with the dividend when dividing by numbers greater or less than 1.

topics.title: Look Before You Leap!

concepts.learning_objective: Apply the rules of divisibility by 4, 100 and 400 to decide leap years.
Use decimal multiplication to compare calendar days with the Earth's actual revolution time.

topics.title: Statistical questions and statements

concepts.learning_objective: Identify a statistical question as one that is answered by collecting data that varies.
Recognise a statistical statement as a claim or summary expressed through numbers, proportions, probabilities or predictions.

topics.title: The arithmetic mean as a fair share

concepts.learning_objective: Calculate the arithmetic mean as the sum of the values divided by the number of values.
Interpret the mean as the equal share each member would get if the total were shared equally.
Distinguish a value of zero from a missing value when counting the number of values for a mean.

topics.title: Describing and comparing data with dot plots

concepts.learning_objective: Describe and compare data using its minimum, maximum, total, average and the difference between maximum and minimum.
Read and interpret a dot plot to see how data is clustered or spread out.

topics.title: Outliers and the median

concepts.learning_objective: Find the median of sorted data with an odd or an even number of values.
Explain how an outlier affects the mean much more than the median.

topics.title: Of ends and the essence: centre and variability

concepts.learning_objective: Use the mean and median as measures of central tendency to describe the centre of data.
Describe the variability of data using its extremes and the spread between them.

topics.title: Visualising data with clustered column graphs

concepts.learning_objective: Read and explain a clustered (double) column graph that compares categories side by side.
Use the scale of a graph to convert bar lengths into values.
Make sense of a graph by first identifying what is given and then inferring from it.

topics.title: Data detective: stories in data

concepts.learning_objective: Read a data table to compare values and spot trends across ages and years.
Judge whether a conclusion can be justified or generalised from the data given.

topics.title: The perpendicular bisector of a line segment

concepts.learning_objective: Define bisection and the perpendicular bisector, and justify the eye construction using congruent triangles.
Use the fact that every point equidistant from X and Y lies on the perpendicular bisector of XY.
Construct the perpendicular bisector of a segment with an unmarked ruler and a compass and explain which conditions are necessary.

topics.title: A 90 degree angle at a point and rope methods of the Sulba-Sutras
topics.ncert_sections: 6.1 (Construction of a 90 degree Angle at a Given Point; Construction Methods in Sulba-Sutras)

concepts.learning_objective: Construct a 90 degree angle at a point on a line, or a perpendicular from a point outside it, using the perpendicular bisector method.
Describe the Sulba-Sutra rope construction of a perpendicular bisector and justify why it works.

topics.title: Angle bisection

concepts.learning_objective: Bisect any angle with a ruler and compass and justify the method by the SSS congruence condition.
Obtain angles such as 45, 22.5 and 75 degrees by combining constructed angles with bisection.

topics.title: Copying an angle and drawing parallel lines
topics.ncert_sections: 6.1 (Repeating Units and Repeating Angles; Construction of a Line Parallel to the Given Line)

concepts.learning_objective: Make an exact copy of a given angle with a ruler and compass and justify it by SSS congruence.
Construct a line parallel to a given line through a point by copying a corresponding angle.

topics.title: Arch designs
topics.ncert_sections: 6.1 (Arch Designs: Trefoil Arch; A Pointed Arch)

concepts.learning_objective: Construct symmetric support lines for trefoil and pointed arches using equal angles and equal lengths.
Identify the line of symmetry of an arch design and predict the effect of unequal support lines.

topics.title: Regular hexagons, the 60 degree angle and related constructions
topics.ncert_sections: 6.1 (Regular Hexagons; Construction of a 60 degree angle; Related Constructions)

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why six congruent equilateral triangles fit around a point to form a regular hexagon.
Construct a 60 degree angle through an equilateral triangle and use it to obtain 120, 30 and 15 degree angles.
Reason with angles to show that the points of a six-pointed star built on a regular hexagon are equilateral triangles.

topics.title: Tangrams and tiling a region with 2 x 1 tiles

concepts.learning_objective: State what tiling is and recall the tangram as a set of seven pieces cut from a square.
Decide whether an m x n grid can be tiled with 2 x 1 tiles by counting unit squares.

topics.title: The black-and-white colouring argument and tiling the plane

concepts.learning_objective: Use black-and-white colouring to prove that a region cannot be tiled with 2 x 1 tiles.
Identify regular polygons that tile the plane and explain this using the angles that meet at a point.

topics.title: Find the unknowns: balances and equations

concepts.learning_objective: Find an unknown weight on a balanced scale, including by removing equal weights from both plates.
Frame an equation using a letter-number for an unknown quantity in a balance or pattern problem.
Identify an equation as a statement of equality between two expressions with an LHS and an RHS.

topics.title: Trial and error and the same-operation property

concepts.learning_objective: Solve a simple equation by substituting values until the LHS equals the RHS.
Explain that performing the same operation on both sides keeps an equation true.
Use addition-subtraction and multiplication-division as inverse operations to evaluate expressions.

topics.title: Solving equations systematically

concepts.learning_objective: Move a term to the other side of an equation as its additive inverse.
Remove a factor or divisor from one side by dividing or multiplying the other side.
Solve equations with the unknown on both sides and recognise an equation with no solution.

topics.title: Solving problems with equations

concepts.learning_objective: Use the rule of a pattern to form and solve an equation for a position number.
Model a real-life situation with an equation in one unknown and interpret the solution.
Model a think-of-a-number trick algebraically to recover the starting number.

topics.title: Generating equations

concepts.learning_objective: Check whether a given value is the solution of an equation and write equations with a given solution.
Build chains of equations by the same operation on both sides, all sharing one solution.
Describe a real-life situation that an equation models.

topics.title: Mind the mistake, mend the mistake

concepts.learning_objective: Find errors in signs when terms are moved across the equal sign.
Correct a faulty solution step and find the right value of the unknown.

topics.title: A pinch of history

concepts.learning_objective: Recall the origin of bijaganita and the word algebra, and the roles of Brahmagupta and Al-Khwarizmi.
Read an equation written in ancient Indian notation with ya and ru.
Apply Brahmagupta's formula x = (D - B)/(A - C) and solve historical problems.
